profile.entities: Centum Electronics Ltd (Parent); Centum Canada (Discontinued); Centum France (Discontinued/Redressement Judiciaire)
profile.subseg: Build-to-Spec (BTS) Defense/Aerospace; Semiconductor Equipment EMS; Industrial Electrification
profile.themes: Overseas Subsidiary Exit; Indigenous Radar Sovereignty; Semiconductor Supply Chain Shift

bull_bear.body: Strategic exit from non-core overseas assets (Canada wind-up, France court-supervised sale with zero expected realization); focus shifted entirely to scaling India ESDM platform; healthy balance sheet supports organic growth.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Supply chain bottlenecks (Copper Clad Laminate, memory chips) extending PCB lead times; Execution delays in long-cycle BTS programs; Geopolitical logistics disruptions (Middle East); Margin pressure if EMS mix remains dominant.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Decisive and optimistic; emphasized 'cleaner' financial visibility post-restructuring; confident in 25-30% standalone growth trajectory despite near-term margin mix headwinds.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The INR 203 Cr impairment is a non-cash accounting event related to discontinued ops, masking the true cash profitability of the continuing India business; Management bandwidth release from overseas fires will accelerate BTS order booking in FY27/FY28 rather than immediate revenue spike due to long development cycles.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Total Borrowings to Equity (standalone) has trended 0.37x (FY24) -> 0.17x (FY25) -> 0.28x (FY26), indicating a generally low and range-bound leverage profile.
- Adjusted ROCE (standalone) was 15.80% (FY24), 12.49% (FY25) and 21.32% (FY26), with the company-at-a-glance slide separately citing 21% FY26 ROCE.
- Adjusted Net Working Capital Days were 141 (FY24), 159 (FY25) and 142 (FY26).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: BTS Revenue +37% YoY (driven by space payloads, radar, missile subsystems); EMS Revenue +21% YoY (semiconductor equipment ramp, industrial electrification); BTS is ~28% of revenue but >50% of order book; EMS acts as annuity business with 6-9 month execution cycles.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply chain tightness in CCL and memory components impacting lead times | Centum Electronics Ltd | beneficiary | High | Diversified sourcing (India/Europe/China) and proactive inventory management mitigating bottlenecks better than pure-play assemblers; high-reliability defense contracts less price-sensitive. |
| Global semiconductor OEMs seeking non-China manufacturing bases | Centum Electronics Ltd | beneficiary | High | Existing ramp with anchor customer validates capability; new discussions underway; positioned as key beneficiary of 'China+1' in high-mix low-volume semiconductor equipment. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Trusted partner for Defence & Strategic Electronics and High-Reliability Electronics Manufacturing, serving domestic and global OEMs across Defence, Aerospace, Industrial, Transportation and Medical sectors; positioned in segments where partner selection is driven by reliability, qualification pedigree and platform trust, not only cost.
- Deep customer stickiness: 30% of revenue comes from customer relationships of 20+ years and 40% from 10-20 year relationships; average customer-group relationships of 10-15 years; single-source supplier for approximately 70-80% of manufactured products (cited as 70% on the company overview slide and ~80% on the competitive-advantage slide).
- High entry barriers built through MIL/space-grade compliance, IPC Class 3 standards, traceability and rigorous quality systems, plus specialized infrastructure across PCBA, box-build, LRUs and systems integration.
- Holds sector-specific quality/security certifications - ISO13485 (Medical), IATF16949 (Automotive), ISO27001 (Information Security) - and SAMAR L5, described as the highest-level certification for DRDO tenders, reinforcing barriers to entry across regulated end-markets.
- 17 patents granted and 125+ publications, underscoring a design/engineering-led moat spanning concept, design, validation, testing and lifecycle support.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Subsidiary Exit - France RJ/Liquidation] Centum T&S Group S.A. and its overseas French subsidiaries entered Redressement Judiciaire (RJ) proceedings in Q4-FY26; management provided for related goodwill, intangibles and inventory and classified the business as discontinued operations in FY26. On 4 June 2026 the French court approved transfer of substantially all operating businesses/employees to successful bidders; Centum concluded loss of control on that date and deconsolidated the entities under Ind-AS 110, recognising a profit on deconsolidation of INR 943 Mn. On 2 July 2026 the process was converted to Liquidation Judiciaire with a judicial liquidator appointed to oversee wind-down.
- [Recognition] Received a Strategic Partner Award from a leading global Industrial/Energy conglomerate for Grid Automation Solutions in Q1-FY27.
- [Shareholding, as of 30 June 2026] Promoter 46.82%, DIIs 19.67%, FIIs 3.31%, Public 30.20%.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: BTS margins ~20% EBITDA; EMS margins 9-11% (cost-plus pressure); FY26 blended margin 12.4% dragged by EMS product mix; improvement expected as BTS mix rises and operating leverage kicks in.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Medium-term revenue CAGR 25-30% (standalone); EBITDA margin target 13-15% over next 1-2 years; FY27 Capex INR 40-45 Cr (50%+ for BTS R&D); No further exceptional losses expected post-deconsolidation of EU unit by Q1/Q2 FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: INR 1,645 Cr standalone (+23% YoY); BTS segment ~INR 800 Cr; Key wins include INR 570 Cr HAL AESA radar (INR 67 Cr dev phase over 2 yrs, remainder to FY30/31) and INR 30 Cr space debris tracking radar.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Scaling indigenous radar systems (AESA, long-range surveillance); Deepening semiconductor equipment OEM partnerships amid global supply chain diversification; Potential 40-60% revenue split shift toward higher-margin BTS by FY28.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Centum has surgically separated its high-growth, high-margin India standalone business (25% revenue CAGR) from loss-making overseas units via discontinued operations, unlocking a pure-play exposure to India's defense radar and semiconductor equipment boom with a record INR 1,645 Cr order book.

open.item: Recommendation of a Final Dividend of ₹ 5 per equity share (50%) for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, subject to shareholder approval.
Recommend a final dividend of ₹5 per equity share (50%) for FY26, subject to shareholder approval.
About INR40 crore capex planned in FY26 (Indian standalone only; no subsidiary capex), taking gross block to ~INR390-400 crore.
Emerging supply-chain lead-time increases in copper-clad laminate (PCBs) and memory components (AI data-center pull), being actively mitigated and monitored through FY27.
No net realization expected from the European asset sale (liabilities held for disposal exceed assets by over INR100 crores); no further write-down expected to hit consolidated books.
Booked ~INR400-470 cr of standalone BTS orders in FY26 (entering FY27 with ~INR800 cr BTS orders); ~INR100-150 cr of spillover orders expected to be booked in Q1/Q2 FY27.

Overseas subsidiaries (already discontinued operations) expected to be fully deconsolidated by end of Q1FY27 (worst case Q2), with no exceptional/one-time losses expected in FY27 consolidated financials.
Canada operations discontinued in Q4FY26 (wind-up in progress); French subsidiary in court-supervised redressement judiciaire, divestment expected substantially concluded by July 2026.
FY27 capex expected around INR40-45 crores, roughly half or slightly more toward BTS R&D capabilities.
Standalone net-block asset turn ~6-7x currently, expected to move to ~8-9x in the next year or two as capex adds capacity (gross block turn ~5x).
Standalone/combined EBITDA margin targeted at 13%-15% over the next 1-2 years (with upside as operating leverage builds).
Semiconductor-equipment EMS revenue progressing broadly in line with expectations toward a ~USD 30 million annual run-rate over the next 2-3 years (anchor-customer led).
Secured HAL UHM-platform AESA radar program worth over INR570 crores over the life cycle; ~INR66-67 cr development phase over 2 years, remaining ~INR500+ cr executed out to FY30/FY31.
Signed MOU with GRSE for aircraft-onto-ship navigation systems, a ~INR500-600 crore opportunity over about five years (orders in yearly parts).
Conclude the Redressement Judiciaire proceedings for Centum T&S Group S.A. and certain underlying overseas subsidiaries.
Complete the liquidation of Centum E&S, Canada, and Centum T&S, Canada, step-down subsidiaries.

Utilize the QIP proceeds of ₹2,100 million in accordance with the objects of the issue.
Medium-term standalone/combined revenue growth target of 25%-30%.
